energy-deficit.short: Energy used minus energy eaten, when the gap is positive. The body covers it from its stores: mostly fat, plus glycogen and a little protein.

dietary-recall.short: Asking people afterwards what they ate and drank. Cheap and easy in a race, but memory errors make it miss or misjudge some intake.

eigs.short: The set of gut changes hard, long exercise causes: damage to the gut lining, a leakier gut, slower emptying and poorer absorption, with or without symptoms.

i-fabp.short: A protein found inside the cells lining the small intestine. When those cells are damaged it leaks into the blood, so a rise in blood I-FABP marks gut-cell damage.

intestinal-permeability.short: How easily things pass through the gut wall into the blood. A rise means a leakier gut barrier, which can let bacterial fragments (endotoxin) into the blood.

fodmap.short: Short-chain carbohydrates the small intestine absorbs poorly (some sugars and sugar alcohols, found in wheat, onions, beans, some fruit and milk). Gut bacteria ferment them, making gas.

taste-fatigue.short: Going off a food or flavour after eating it again and again, as many athletes do with sweet gels and drinks late in long races.
